Ofsted judged Meadows School to be Outstanding for Personal Development and Sixth-Form Provision, and Good for Quality of Education, Behaviour & Attitudes, and Leadership & Management. Inspectors praised the school "as a place where pupils feel safe, are proud of their achievements, and benefit from staff who are ambitious for their future.”
Meadows School is a non-maintained special day school in Kent run by the children’s charity Barnardo’s. We provide education for students between 7 and 18 who have an EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan) or are in the process of obtaining one. Our designation is for pupils with Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs.
Our site is in Southborough (between the two historic towns of Tunbridge Wells and Tonbridge) on a beautiful 19-acre campus with capacity for up to 100 pupils.
The pupils who attend Meadows school may have had a negative experience of education and some will have spent time out of school in the past. It is for this reason that we have the three values of 'Engage, Enrich, Empower' at our core.
We engage minds, enrich lives, and empower futures.
We strive to achieve a culture that: promotes respect, tolerance and kindness; celebrates success and provides the ability to work through difficulties. Working in partnership with families and agencies, we aim to support pupils to develop character strengths and promote their resilience to enable the young person to maximise their potential during their time with us.
We offer a broad curriculum tailored to individual pupils needs. There are opportunities to study for GCSEs, BTEC, Functional Skills, Vocational Skills qualifications, Entry Level Certificates and Open Awards.
We believe in children; We transform lives; We fulfil vision.
Why Choose Us
​​​​​​​Excellent facilities​​​​​​​
The school sits on a beautiful 19-acre site with its own ancient woodland set between the two historic towns of Tunbridge Wells and Tonbridge in Kent.
Well-Developed Behaviour Management
Meadows School provides a holistic approach to individual behaviour and well-being working closely with parents and carers.
Bespoke, Broad and Balanced Curriculum
A bespoke curriculum is provided which can engage individual pupils in education and enrich school experience with new and challenging opportunities. This will empower them to move on to the next step of their education and careers, and ultimately to lead independent lives.
Pupils feel valued at Meadows School. They know that their social, emotional and mental health (SEMH) needs will be understood and supported.

pageCache.pageTitle: Meadows School - Building Careers with Fernham Homes
pageCache.text:
Building Careers with Fernham Homes
As part of Careers Week at Meadows School, students took part in an engaging and hands-on session with Sean Ellis, Ben Stone, and Kay Martin from Fernham Homes, exploring the world of construction and the skills needed to succeed in the industry.
The session covered routes into construction, including apprenticeships, traineeships, and college pathways. Students learned about the importance of personal skills such as communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and forming positive relationships, as well as the range of salaries across different construction roles. The speakers emphasised the critical role of health and safety on-site, ensuring every project is completed safely.
Students also took part in an interactive activity ordering the use of materials in a house build, putting their new knowledge into practice. At the end of the session, pupils shook hands with the speakers to show their gratitude, highlighting the value of professional etiquette alongside technical skills.
It was an informative and interactive session, giving students valuable insights into construction careers. Thank you, Sean, Ben, and Kay, for sharing your expertise and helping our students lay the foundations for their futures!

pageCache.pageTitle: Meadows School - Sparking Interest with Peter Costello
pageCache.text:
Sparking Interest with Peter Costello
During Careers Week at Meadows School, students enjoyed a hands-on session with Peter Costello from Tunbridge Wells Repair Café, exploring the ethical and financial benefits of repairing broken household items rather than replacing them.
Peter brought along a radio he had mended, magnet-powered electrics, and a tool which measured resistance, demonstrating how readings differed between staff and students. This practical activity sparked curiosity and showed the science behind everyday objects in a fun, interactive way.
He also highlighted the value of volunteering for community initiatives, explaining how giving time to projects like the Repair Café not only helps others but builds skills, confidence, and connections.
The session left students inspired to think about sustainability, practical skills, and community contribution. Thank you, Peter, for sharing your expertise, showing the power of repair, and encouraging students to make a positive impact in their communities!

pageCache.pageTitle: Meadows School - Taking Off to New Careers with Kathleen Cameron
pageCache.text:
Taking Off to New Careers with Kathleen Cameron
As part of Careers Week at Meadows School, students were inspired by Kathleen Cameron, a female pilot with easyJet, who shared her experiences of working in aviation.
Kathleen spoke about the wide range of jobs within the aviation industry, the training required to become a pilot, and what a typical day in the role can involve. Students were captivated by video footage that gave them an exciting insight into commercial aviation and the responsibilities involved in flying passenger aircraft.
The session highlighted the skills, dedication, and opportunities available in aviation, inspiring students to consider careers in this fast-paced and global industry.
Thank you to Kathleen for sharing her expertise, motivating our students, and inspiring them to aim high as they explore future careers!

pageCache.pageTitle: Meadows School - Young Arts Project: A Celebration of Southborough Common
pageCache.text:
Young Arts Project: A Celebration of Southborough Common
Vice chair, Elaine Johnson, The Arts Society, Sevenoaks, made contact with the assistant headteacher, Camilla Doonan, whilst researching the history of Meadows School for Southborough Society.
Having been on a tour of the school and seen the wonderful art facilities and the potential for art as a meditative and nurturing medium, she proposed that the school was worthy of The Arts Society Sevenoaks' support. Our Young Arts co-ordinator, Anne Deane, took over and led a very valuable project with Claire Clements, a community artist, working with students of a range of ages.
The school is run by Barnardo’s charity, and the students have high-level educational and emotional needs, so this sort of work is highly relevant.
The aim of the project was to produce a textile wall hanging entitled: A celebration of Southborough Common.
The students began their creative journey by taking photos of scenery and nature found on the Common.
Artworks were then created using a variety of art processes based on the photos taken.
The final sessions saw the children experimenting with appliqué, creating beautiful fabric flowers and leaves.
Children developed their cutting and sewing skills to create simple motifs and to practice skills of co-operation.
The final result is a spectacular wall hanging that celebrates nature in a local environment as well as a sense of place.
Claire hopes to display it in Southborough Library and at one of our lectures next Autumn.

Careers
Excellent careers education, advice and guidance, help pupils to be very well-prepared for future life (Ofsted 2024)
We aim to ensure that:
The government has introduced the following mandatory guidance for schools – called The Gatsby Benchmarks:
1. A stable careers programme 2. Learning from career and labour market information 3. Addressing the needs of each student 4. Linking curriculum learning to careers 5. Encounters with employers and employees 6. Experiences of workplaces 7. Encounters with further and higher education 8. Personal guidance
Careers education starts in KS2 with "The Working World" part of the 1Decision PSHCE programme.
All pupils have the opportunity to take part in "Meadows Careers Week" each year when lessons across the curriculum are involved in delivering information on different careers or guidance linked with that subject and external business people in a variety of jobs and industries come to meet and chat to our pupils.
The KS3 careers programme is explored through Independent Living Skills within PSHCE and their participation in the whole school's "Careers Week". From April 2022, years 7,8 & 9 can apply for access to an independent impartial career advisor. From year 7 onwards, Link Workers will support the use of online quizzes to help guide our young people into making informed career choices.
KS4 pupils have automatic access to an independent, impartial career advisor in both years 10 and 11. The pupils have lessons in 'Life Beyond School' where discussion begins around transition to the next phase of their journey post 16. Pupils also participate in the whole school "Careers Week." Individual Link Workers support any workplace experiences, along with transitions on to Sixth Form, College or Apprenticeships.
The KS5 PSHCE careers programme covers "Money: preparing for the unknown", "journey towards financial independence", "to borrow or not to borrow" and BTEC qualifications, which cover topics such as:
Under the Department for Education’s update of the school's "Careers guidance Aug 2022", years 7,8 & 9 can now have access to a meeting with an independent impartial Careers Advisor. An annual email will be sent to parents and carers requesting you to apply for a meeting on behalf of your child.
'Pupils of all ages benefit from the school’s excellent approach to careers information, advice and guidance.' (Ofsted 2024)

Curriculum Intent
At Meadows School, our curriculum intent is to provide a broad, balanced, and challenging education that prepares our pupils for a rapidly changing world. We believe that every pupil deserves an education that fosters their intellectual, creative, emotional, and physical development, and that provides them with the skills, knowledge, and values necessary to succeed in life. Our curriculum is designed to be individualised, inclusive, and relevant to the needs and interests of our pupils, and is underpinned by our school values of engage, enrich, and empower. Through our curriculum, we aim to inspire a love of learning that will stay with our pupils throughout their lives, and equip them with the confidence and skills to achieve their full potential.
'Adults adapt each pupil’s curriculum well to meet their specific SEMH needs.' (Ofsted 2024)

pageCache.pageTitle: Meadows School - Marching Towards Success with Kevin Midmore
pageCache.text:
Marching Towards Success with Kevin Midmore
As part of Careers Week at Meadows School, students enjoyed an inspiring and hands-on session with Kevin Midmore, who shared his experiences of a career in the army.
Kevin spoke about the opportunities the army provides, including making lifelong friends, travelling the world, and pursuing hobbies. He engaged pupils with practical activities such as trying camo face paint, crawling under camouflage nets, and exploring his 4x4 truck, which had travelled to Ukraine to supply humanitarian aid.
Students were fascinated when Kevin showed his medals and gave each pupil a Victoria Cross keepsake, making the session memorable and personal. His talk highlighted the discipline, teamwork, and adventure that come with a career in the armed forces.
Thank you, Kevin, for sharing your experiences, inspiring our students, and showing how dedication and courage can lead to an extraordinary career!

Full Steam Ahead with Train Driver Marcus Baker
As part of Careers Week at Meadows School, students enjoyed an exciting and interactive session with Marcus Baker, a train driver on the Thameslink lines, who shared insights into his career and daily work.
Marcus explained the application stages for becoming a train driver, including the required tests, skills, and safety knowledge. He also talked about timetables, shift work, and the responsibilities involved in keeping passengers safe and trains running smoothly.
A highlight of the session was when students had the chance to try a train driving simulator, giving them a hands-on experience of what it’s like to operate a train and manage real-world challenges on the tracks.
The session offered students a clear view of a unique and vital career, combining technical skills, focus, and responsibility.
Thank you, Marcus, for sharing your expertise, giving students a thorough insight into train driving, and inspiring them to keep their careers full steam ahead!

pageCache.text:
No Problem! Meadows staff rise to the challenge
Through a series of engaging and thought-provoking challenges, colleagues worked together to solve problems, think differently and strengthen the relationships that help make Meadows such a positive and supportive place to learn and work. The activities focused on collaboration, resilience and effective communication—skills that sit at the heart of both great teamwork and great teaching.
The day also provided an opportunity for staff to reflect on our shared purpose:
“We engage minds, enrich lives, and empower futures.”
As highlighted in our School Purpose statement, we believe in creating a nurturing community where everyone is empowered to embrace their unique journey. The challenges reminded us that, just like our students, we achieve the most when we work together, support one another and approach obstacles with curiosity and confidence.
A huge thank you to Liam and Imogen from The Problem Solving Company for an enjoyable and inspiring day that left us with plenty of ideas, smiles and strengthened connections across the Meadows team.
After all, when it comes to problem-solving at Meadows, every challenge is an opportunity to grow.

Ofsted Report
Meadows School was last inspected by Ofsted in November 2024.
We are delighted to share the fantastic news that our recent Section 5 Ofsted inspection has been a tremendous success. The inspection team highlighted a combination of good and outstanding judgments across the school, a reflection of the exceptional efforts and dedication of our entire school community.
This result is a celebration of what we can achieve together as a community. We will continue to build on this success, striving to reach even greater heights in the future.

Pupil Premium Funding
Pupil Premium is funding provided by the Government to help schools reduce inequalities for eligible pupils. Funding is available for children in care, children who have been adopted from Local Authority care, children who are eligible for Free School Meals and children from service families.
Schools can use Pupil Premium funding to support a range of projects, interventions and additional provision. This may benefit individual eligible pupils as well as other pupils where the provision supports wider educational needs. Funding may also be combined with the school’s main budget where appropriate.
Schools are required to publish information about the Pupil Premium funding they receive and how it is used. Meadows School’s Pupil Premium Statement, setting out our approach, priorities and planned expenditure, can be read in full below.
Funding for children in care is managed differently. It is allocated through the relevant Local Authority and is usually administered by the Virtual School responsible for the child. The use of this funding is discussed between the school and the relevant Local Authority as part of the pupil’s Personal Education Plan (PEP) meetings and is based on the individual needs of the child.
Provision mapping is being developed for potentially eligible pupils to ensure that individual needs and barriers to learning are identified and understood. Pupil Premium funding will be used to provide targeted support according to identified need, which may include additional equipment, 1:1 support and targeted educational support.
The impact of this provision will be monitored and reviewed to ensure that it is making a positive difference to pupils’ learning, progress and wider outcomes. This forms part of the school’s wider approach to inclusion and improving outcomes for disadvantaged pupils.
The school’s approach to personal development is exceptional (Ofsted 2024)

The Pupil Experience
We know it can be a bit scary when you change schools so we try and give you as much information as possible before you start. You will have visited the school already and maybe had some taster days so that you have some idea of what to expect.
On your first day you will have an 'Admission Meeting' which involves you, your parents/carers and staff who you will work with. This would usually include your Tutor and Link Worker. You will also be given a 'new student' booklet appropriate to the year group you will be joining.
You'll get to meet your new classmates and receive your new timetable.
Read what our students have said about us below.
Sy, Former student
The most impactful thing Meadows ever did was the support from all the staff. For me, the support meant you didn't have to just rely on yourself. That's what gave me a chance.
A leaving statement from a 6th form student
I feel that Meadows has been my second home for the last eleven years. I have felt safe, heard and understood. Meadows' staff have always guided me to take new opportunities to develop my skills and abilities, including helping me get into college. I have just achieved Level 3 Car Mechanics and I will always be grateful to Meadows.
Leaving statement from a 6th form student
I have enjoyed my time at Meadows School. The staff have been kind, helpful and persevered with me and provided a timetable to suit my learning needs and style in a safe environment. Thanks to the support, I have gained my GCSE's, and I am now a more confident person.
The Pupil Experience

16+ Provision
Provision in the sixth form is especially strong. (OFSTED - Outstanding 2024)
Our 16+ programme (Key Stage 5) is situated in Broomfield House on the secondary school campus, though it is separate from key stage 3 and 4.
We offer personalised bespoke study programmes tailored to each student’s skills, interests, abilities, and existing qualifications. Alongside a broad and balanced academic experience, we provide a robust enrichment programme featuring activities such as mountain biking, bowling, and kayaking. Additionally, we offer link worker support, the Duke of Edinburgh Award to further enrich our students' educational and personal development and life skills, including preparation for the driving theory test and some driving lessons.
Each student’s pathway is designed to ensure they gain the knowledge and skills needed to thrive, stay resilient, and find fulfilment in their future endeavours.
We warmly invite prospective students to visit our sixth form to explore first-hand how we can support their unique educational journey.
For more details, please see the documents below.

About Us
Placements at Meadows School include the students themselves expressing their wish to attend Meadows School.
Students' interests and hobbies can often be a stepping stone to engage them with education and provide opportunities for success.
Provision of an allocated pastoral link worker to work with every student and their parents/carers throughout their time at the school.
Enrichment activities are part of everyday life at Meadows School. Students are able to try new activities, and develop skills and confidence in the classroom and beyond.
Key working sessions offer opportunities for visits and off-site activities and can include independent living skills.
Access to the school's well-being services, which include Speech and Language therapy, Counselling and Occupational Therapy.
Students are made to feel included and a part of the school from the moment they start at Meadows School and are involved in target setting and progress reviews.
Celebrating achievements through school assemblies, weekly and annual prize-giving ceremonies
Students can achieve success in a variety of areas, from nationally-recognised accreditations to school awards.
To assist students in celebrating their ability, race, religion, colour, culture, gender, family network and community for life in a diverse society.
To provide a broad, balanced and differentiated curriculum to include the National Curriculum, which encourages every student to acquire high standards of knowledge, skills and understanding relevant to adult life and the worlds of work and leisure.
To encourage each student to develop to their true potential.
To develop self-esteem and a good personal image yet be sensitive to the needs of others.
To help each student to become happy, independent, caring people, capable of making a contribution to both society and the community.
From the time of admission to Meadows School, each student is treated as an individual with their own specific needs. After a period of review and assessment, the school prepares an Individual Risk Assessment and Crisis Support Plan, Provision Plan and Individual Care Plan, if appropriate.
Many students placed at the school will need considerable adult agency support.

These usually take place in school and the appropriate individuals are invited to attend. For students who are causing concern, additional meetings might also be convened in order that specific objectives can be reviewed or targets set.

Yes, informal visits are organised by our Admissions Officer and are strictly by appointment only. Visits typically take place on Tuesdays and Thursdays at either 9:30 or 11:15. If these times/days aren't convenient for you, please do not hesitate to get in touch. Please allow 40 minutes for your visit.
If you would like to book a visit, please contact us on 01892 529144 or by email enquiries@meadowsschool.org.uk. Please note that informal visits are purely for parents/carers to gather information about the school, so we ask that students do not attend the visit at this time.
We also offer formal visits (which the student can attend) but these are offered by us once we have received a formal consultation from the local authority and our panel feel that we may potentially be able to meet the needs of the student.
